newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST- Australian General News - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST- Australian General News - Nov 13.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Although Prime Minister John Howard conceded yesterday that the Federal Government's media review would look at changes to foreign investment policy, he suggested there was a very strong feeling in the community that the current levels of foreign ownership in Australia were already high enough, despite calls from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and media companies such as Rupert Murdoch's News Ltd to abolish cross-media ownership and foreign investment restrictions. Page 1.

Speaking on Melbourne's Radio 3AW, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday defended his handling of the race debate and reaffirmed his commitment to an open debate in Australia on immigration levels. Howard strongly rejected suggestion by former Prime Miniser Paul Keating that his approach to the debate represented a return to the "White Australia" immigration policy. Page 2.

Independent Senator Brian Harradine said yesterday his gut feeling was to reject the proposed partial sale of Telstra, believing it to be worth double its A$24 billion price tag. Harradine suggested the Government further examine Telstra's worth, but coneded it was perfectly clear it had a mandate to raise A$8 billion by selling a third of the telecommunications carrier. Page 3.

Federal Cabinet is looking at controls on the cable rollout by telecommunications carriers Telstra and Optus in an attempt to satisfy Coalition backbenchers who are upset about visual pollution in leafy suburbs. Communications Minister Richard Alston has discussed a radical plan with at least one of the carriers to halt all aerial cabling in cases where the carriers had not yet submitted Prescribed Activity Notices with local councils, yet this proposal has been abandoned. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a move which would virtually wipe out all of the Government's planned tax rebate for people with private health insurance, Australia's largest health fund, Medibank Private, has applied for increases in premiums averaging 15 per cent across all States. Increases of about 15 per cent would boost the monthly cost of insurance for couples and families with top hospital cover by at least A$15 and lump singles with top hospital cover with a rise of up to A$100 a year. Page 1.

Following a 15-month investigation commissioned by the former Labor Government, the Economic Planning Advisory Commission's childcare taskforce releases its final report today, recommending the abolition of all current funding mechanisms for childcare, the introduction of a single payment made directly to parents through a swipe card system, the doubling of parental leave to two years and forcing schools to offer after hours care. Page 1.

Responding to calls by News Limited and Fairfax to lift controls on foreign media ownership, Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday that the Government would have to consider changing foreign ownership limits as part of its review of media policy, but here was a strong feeling in the community that the levels of foreign media ownership were already too high. Page 1.

In his 21-page interim report, police royal commissioner Justice James Wood recommended a legislative overhaul of the New South Wales police, suggesting that the New South Wales Police Board be abolished and powers to hire, sack and transfer officers be gven to the new State police commissioner Peter Ryan. The report also recommended that police officers undergo random drug, alcohol and integrity tests and provide financial statements every three years. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following yesterday's announcement by New South Wales Premier Bob Carr that the State Government had agreed to recommendations of the police royal commissioner Justice James Wood, the chairman of the outgoing Police Board, Don Mackay, accused the Governmet of using a "knee-jerk reaction" and the police union said the Government was acting with undue haste ahead of necessary public debate, in a move which would vest too much power in the police commissioner's position. Page 1.

Hunter Water Corporation has confirmed that a water sample taken on October 24 from the enclosed Glovers Hill reservoir showed levels of egg-like oocysts of Cryptosporidium parasite many times higher than minimum high levels, which, when ingested, can caue acute gastro-intestinal disease, diarrhoea and vomiting in otherwise healthy people. Page 1.

After a fight broke out between rival gangs at a Hunters Hill High School playground yesterday, a 14-year-old boy was taken to Royal North Shore hospital with a stab wound to the shoulder and another boy is facing drug and malicious wounding charges. The incident was witnessed by pupils as young as 12 and is the second schoolyard stabbing in the past month. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday rejected claims by former Prime Minister Paul Keating that the he had failed to display leadership in the race debate and accused Keating of over-reacting with claims that the debate was about a return to a white Austrlia. Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett said Keating's comments were "intellectually bankrupt", too late to be effective and totally misguided. Page 3.
THE AGE

There was a major breach of security at a second-hand Government furniture auction last week, where secret cables from Australia's overseas embassies and other official documents were filed in a cabinet that was publicly auctioned at the former headquarters of the Department of Foreign Affairs. Page A1.

The Victorian Parliament has followed the lead of its Federal counterpart by carrying a bipartisan resolution condemning racial intolerance. The motion came amid allegations by Labor MPs of a vicious Asian backlash in Melbourne, that included death threas, assaults, and the work of Asian students being marked down. Page A1.

A blast at the Australian Defence Industries ammunitions factory in Mulwala on the New South Wales-Victoria border has killed one man. The blast was so large, tremors could be felt up to 60 kilometres away and it renewed calls for a safety review of the lant by Defence Industry, Science and Personnel Minister Bronwyn Bishop. Page A1.

High-profile ABC broadcaster Doug Aiton, a radio announcer on radio 3LO, is the latest ABC broadcaster to go off air, following the resignation of 3LO morning and afternoon hosts Peter Couchman and Elaine Canty. Aiton was sacked by station general managr Sue Howard, but he says he believes the decision for his sacking came from ABC management in Sydney. Page A1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
